> [!NOTE]
> Stacked on #61243. Review only the top two commits (`[KV Cache] Address packed kernel blocks…`, `[HiSparse] Fill device pool blocks…`). I'll retarget once #61243 merges.

## Purpose

#61243 sizes the HiSparse indexer group's device-pool block to one 256-token kernel page. On GLM-5.3-Flash, the shared pool block is sized by the 1.18 MB KDA state pages, so each 92,928 B indexer page leaves ~92% of its block as padding.

This PR fills each pool block with as many whole indexer pages as fit (12 on Flash, a 3072-token indexer block):

- `vllm/v1/hisparse/layout.py`: size the indexer group after the hot/resident groups, to whole pages of the largest device-group page.
- `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`: a block that holds 12 pages is no multiple of one page apart, and the previous lcm alignment would inflate it to 4.3 MB. `AttentionGroup.map_kv_cache_to_kernel_blocks` now numbers kernel pages in units of `gcd(block stride, page size)` (kernel block `j` of block `b` = `b * kernel_block_stride + kernel_block_offsets[j]`). The result is unchanged when the block stride is a whole number of pages.

Non-HiSparse runs are unaffected: their packed group layout never splits blocks this way.

The scheduler block grows from 2304 to 9216 tokens on Flash (the lcm of the group block sizes). The prefix-cache hash block is unchanged, and long-context prefix-cache hit rate is unchanged (below).

## Test Plan

Unit tests (CPU):

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py
```

`test_packed_group_kernel_blocks_with_unaligned_block_stride` fails on #61243 (`ValueError` from `map_kv_cache_to_kernel_blocks`).

E2E on 4×B200, TP4, `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash@eb9eb208`, HiSparse `host_pool_gib=200`. Each server ran back to back on the same node.

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --trust-remote-code --language-model-only -tp 4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len {86016,151552} --max-num-seqs 512 \
  --attention-config '{"hisparse_config":{}}' \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":200}}'
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len {65536,131072} --random-output-len 16384 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 256 --ignore-eos --seed 42
```

Accuracy used bf16 KV and the GSM8K client in `tests/evals/gsm8k`. The long-context run used 100-shot prompts with `--kv-cache-memory-bytes 4G` and prefix caching on, so HiSparse offloads to host.

## Test Result

**Throughput** (fp8, c=256). Max concurrency is the HiSparse steady-state figure:

| In/out | Variant | Out tok/s | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | Max concurrency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64k/16k | no HiSparse | 4309 | 295 s | 29.1 ms | 117.5× |
| | #61243 | 3355 | 257 s | 48.4 ms | 157.7× |
| | **this PR** | **3835** | **185 s** | 54.9 ms | **440.7×** |
| 128k/16k | no HiSparse | 2707 | 634 s | 29.1 ms | 75.0× |
| | #61243 | 2379 | 619 s | 41.6 ms | 102.5× |
| | **this PR** | **2756** | **384 s** | 68.2 ms | **251.6×** |

**Accuracy**:

| Eval | #61243 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K (×2 runs, c=32) | 0.918 / 0.924 | 0.916 / 0.917 |
| GSM8K (c=1) | 0.95 | 0.945 |
| 100-shot, 4 GiB GPU KV | 0.925 / 0.955 | 0.92 / 0.94 |
| Prefix-cache hit rate (100-shot) | 98.0% | 98.6% |

Capacity on H200 (bf16, 139k-token requests, steady-state): #61243 59.2×, this PR 136.9×.

Per-step decode cost (TPOT) is still above no-HiSparse runs. That is a separate follow-up.
